findings.description: Once `pup-gate` is required, an open PR that an older pup gated (head still at the pin, no status) cannot be merged. `planRegate` refuses to re-gate it with "nothing new to gate… Merge it on GitHub", which GitHub now blocks. The new docs forbid setting the status by hand, so nothing can unblock it.
findings.body:
**This change leaves PRs gated before decision 182 with no way to merge.**

Take a session that a pre-182 `pup merge --pr` moved to `merged` while its PR is still open. That is the normal state: LOOP.md says `merged` means the PR exists, not that GitHub merged it. Its head is still at the pinned sha, and no `pup-gate` status was ever set on that sha.

After the operator runs the decision-182 protection setup, GitHub turns the merge button off, admins included because `enforce_admins` is on. LOOP.md's fix is to re-gate with `pup merge <task> --pr`. For a `merged` session, `planMerge` routes that through `planRegate`, which refuses when the head equals the pin:

```ts
if (pr.head === pinned) {
  throw new Error(
    `${prUrl} still has its head at ${pinned}, the commit the gate pinned: there is nothing ` +
      `new to gate. Merge it on GitHub, then run \`pup land ...\`. ` + NOT_REGATED,
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4b89b5e96e7c351c2bfecf087d5af448bef9540e/src/core/regate.service.ts#L123-L129

That error tells the operator to merge on GitHub, which protection now forbids. The docs also get these PRs wrong:

- LOOP.md L63-64 says a missing status means "its head moved after the gate", but these heads never moved.
- LOOP.md L65 says "Never set the status by hand", which rules out the only manual fix.
- `pup land` needs a PR GitHub has already merged, so it cannot help.
- The `findOpenPullRequest` first-gate path, which would reach `setGateStatus`, runs only for `awaiting-review` sessions.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4b89b5e96e7c351c2bfecf087d5af448bef9540e/skills/pup/LOOP.md#L62-L65

**Trigger:** any `--pr` PR that is still open when the operator turns protection on. The ADR's "Limits, accepted" section does not mention PRs already in flight.

**Fix, either of:**
- Let a re-gate whose PR head equals the pin set `pup-gate` on it once the head reads back at the pin, instead of refusing.
- Document a one-time migration step, such as merging or closing in-flight `--pr` PRs before turning protection on.

findings.description: On a branch that is protected but has no required status checks, GitHub probably answers `PATCH .../protection/required_status_checks` with 404 "Required status checks not enabled". That would leave no working command for this state except the `PUT`, which the ADR itself says wipes existing protection.
findings.body:
**The setup command for a branch that is protected but has no required checks probably fails.**

The ADR detects this state correctly: `GET .../protection` returns 200 with no `required_status_checks` key. For that state it prescribes:

```sh
gh api --method PATCH repos/OWNER/REPO/branches/TARGET/protection/required_status_checks \
  -F strict=false -f 'contexts[]=pup-gate'
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4b89b5e96e7c351c2bfecf087d5af448bef9540e/docs/adr/0182-pup-merge-pr-sets-a-pup-gate-status-on.md#L43-L49 (the same command is in `skills/pup/LOOP.md` L52-54)

GitHub's "Update status check protection" endpoint (PATCH) changes an existing status-check setting but does not create one. On a protected branch without status checks it returns `404 {"message":"Required status checks not enabled"}`, and `POST .../required_status_checks/contexts` fails the same way. Required status checks have no endpoint that turns them on alone, the way `enforce_admins` does. The REST API turns them on only through the full `PUT .../protection`, and the ADR warns at L29-30 that this PUT replaces any protection the branch already has.

**Trigger:** a target that has, for example, only required reviews. The operator runs the documented PATCH, gets a 404, and the only remaining documented route wipes the review rules.

**Note:** four reviewers independently flagged this from knowledge of the API, and the validator agreed. None of them could make a live call, so please confirm it once on a scratch repo.

**Fix:** for this state, tell the operator to add `pup-gate` as a required check in the branch-protection settings page, which turns status checks on without touching other rules. Alternatively, give a `jq` step that turns the GET output into a full PUT body. That is not a plain copy, because the GET and PUT shapes differ: `enforce_admins.enabled` must become a boolean, and the review and restriction objects must become lists of logins and slugs.

findings.description: SKILL.md (and LOOP.md L60-61) say `enforce_admins` means no admin login can bypass `pup-gate`. That overclaims: a session holding the operator's admin `gh` login can delete `enforce_admins` or post `pup-gate` itself. Say it stops the routine admin bypass, and that `pup land` stays the real check, as the ADR's Limits section already admits.

The `!host || !owner || !name` guard in `setGateStatus` can never fire, because both callers pass `pullRequest.repo` built by `originRepoSlug`, the same value `assertPullRequestHead` just used. Dropping it and its dedicated test removes a branch, and a malformed slug would still fail loudly in `gh`.
